instruction.text: Paul buys a book that costs £13.50 but pays with a £20 note. Work out how much change he should get back.
instruction.sound: Paul buys a book that costs £13.50 but pays with a 20 pound note. Work out how much change he should get back.

instruction.text: Tina receives £30 pocket money every month. She buys a pen for £1.30 and a notebook for £9.60. Work out how much change she should have.

atoms.a: First, add up the <t-yellow>total of the items</t-yellow>.

instruction.text: Next, count up to subtract the <t-yellow>items</t-yellow> from <t-blue>Tina’s pocket money</t-blue>.
Sarah has saved <t-blue>£60</t-blue> and would like to buy a new bike helmet that costs <t-yellow>£38.80</t-yellow>. Count up to work out how much money she will have left after buying the helmet.
Vera goes to the supermarket and spends £73.10. She pays with two £50 notes. Work out how much change she should get back.
instruction.sound: Vera goes to the supermarket and spends £73.10. She pays with 2 50 pound notes. Work out how much change she should get back.

atoms.a: First, calculate the <t-blue>total Vera pays in notes</t-blue>.

instruction.text: Next, count up to subtract <t-blue>her total</t-blue> from the <t-yellow>notes she pays with</t-yellow>.

instruction.text: If Lola and Ben had £1,000, they would adopt a dog from the shelter for £280 and buy him a beautiful basket for £125. They would also buy him lots of food and toys for £140. Work out how much change they should have left.
